Key takeaways A Record-Breaking Descent Spanish skateboarder Diego Poncelet has officially set a new world speed record, reaching a staggering 151.83 km/h (94.34 mph). The 27-year-old athlete achieved this feat in Charlevoix, Quebec, pushing the boundaries of downhill skateboarding

A Record-Breaking Descent

Spanish skateboarder Diego Poncelet has officially set a new world speed record, reaching a staggering 151.83 km/h (94.34 mph). The 27-year-old athlete achieved this feat in Charlevoix, Quebec, pushing the boundaries of downhill skateboarding.

Context and Verification

This high-speed run highlights the extreme nature of downhill skateboarding, a sport that requires immense precision and protective equipment. As velocity increases, the margin for error diminishes, making such records significant milestones in the sport's technical progression. Readers can verify the footage of this historic run directly through the official coverage provided by the BBC.
